title: A Orbit for the Vector
premise: Elodie Eastwick has spent eleven years alone tending Beacon 7, an automated relay whose original owners are long dead, until a nine-second gravity flicker across the system delivers a compressed alien message into her station's core — addressed to her, by name. The message is a ceasefire key from the enemy Vessic species, and both warring human factions will kill to control it: one to end the war, one to bury it. Pursued by a duty-bound naval officer who becomes her reluctant ally and eventual love, Elodie must carry the key through collapsing relay chains to the neutral archive world where it can be broadcast to everyone at once. She succeeds only by sacrificing her own claim to belonging — uploading her memories alongside the message — and in the epilogue's quiet aftermath, the war ends and someone finally comes to relieve the last technician of her post.
about_author: Odile Amberdale is a former radio astronomer who left observatory life to write fiction about the people history forgets to thank. She lives near a decommissioned listening station and still answers signals nobody sends.

chapters.title: The Weight of Routine
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A day in the rhythm of Beacon 7: calibrations, ration logs, conversations with the station's decaying AI, Marrow. We learn she inherited this posting from her mother and has never been relieved. Emotional beat: loneliness worn smooth into comfort, with hairline cracks showing.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Gravity stutters across the entire system; instruments scream; the beacon's core rewrites itself with a compressed packet addressed to EASTWICK, E. The flicker ends as abruptly as it began. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread — the universe just noticed her.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Was For
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, with Marrow's fragmented logs. She excavates the station's buried records and discovers the beacon was built during the war's first year by a joint human-Vessic team — including her grandmother. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed from burden to secret purpose.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Lieutenant Cassian Roe's POV aboard the patrol ship Verity. His orders: any anomalous transmission from Beacon 7 is to be seized and its keeper detained. He arrives expecting a saboteur and finds a tired woman holding something that terrifies him. Emotional beat: duty meeting doubt for the first time.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Prisoners
chapters.summary: Alternating Elodie/Cassian POV. Cassian takes custody of Elodie and the message core, but his second-in-command reports directly to hardline faction command. A standoff in the docking bay leaves them fugitives together on a stolen shuttle. Emotional beat: enemies forced into trust.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Weeks in transit; she teaches Cassian what the message fragment decodes to so far — coordinates, a countdown, the word 'witness.' They argue about whether ending the war is even possible or desirable. Emotional beat: intimacy growing inside argument.

chapters.title: Relay Chain Broken
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Their route requires dead relays; one wakes as they dock, hijacked by faction hunters. A brutal EVA firefight costs them their fuel reserve and Cassian nearly his life. Elodie saves him. Emotional beat: the cost of the mission made flesh.

chapters.title: Vessic Ghost
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A derelict Vessic ship drifts in their path; inside, preserved recordings reveal the ceasefire offer was made years ago and suppressed by both sides. Her grandmother's voice is among the negotiators. Emotional beat: grief for a peace that died unheard.

chapters.title: The Countdown Explained
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marrow, patched remotely into their shuttle, decrypts further: the message must reach the neutral Archive of Thessaly within forty days or the Vessic fleet assumes bad faith and launches. Emotional beat: hope acquiring a deadline.

chapters.title: Port of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Resupply at a smuggler station; an old friend of her mother's offers help, then sells their location. They escape in the chaos but Elodie is wounded. Emotional beat: learning that belonging can be bought by anyone.

chapters.title: What Cassian Carries
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. He confesses he signed the order that destroyed a civilian convoy early in the war; duty was how he survived the guilt. Elodie doesn't forgive him — she tells him guilt means he's still choosing. Emotional beat: love beginning as honesty.

chapters.title: Hunters
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV: Commander Ilsa Vane of the Continuity faction. She reveals the hardliners have known about the ceasefire key for years and built their power on the war's continuation. She dispatches a strike wing. Emotional beat: chilling clarity of conviction without conscience.

chapters.title: Gravity Remembers
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Another nine-second flicker hits — the Vessic checking on their message. It briefly grants Elodie a sensory vision of the enemy: not monsters, but mourners. Emotional beat: the enemy rendered human, the war rendered obscene.

chapters.title: The Choice at Meridian Gate
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Cornered at a jump gate, they can flee to safety or burn their only escape route to draw off pursuit. Cassian chooses to burn it, formally breaking his oath. Emotional beat: duty inverted — loyalty transferred from institution to person and principle.

chapters.title: Thessaly Approach
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The Archive world appears — a library planetoid tended by neutral archivists who refuse to take sides, including in this. They will not broadcast the message unless a living witness attests to its provenance. Emotional beat: sanctuary that demands more than arrival.

chapters.title: Vane Descends
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Vane's strike wing breaches Thessaly's neutrality; the archive burns in sections. Cassian holds a corridor alone while Elodie runs for the broadcast spire. Emotional beat: sacrifice staged against destruction of memory itself.

chapters.title: Witness
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. At the spire, the archivists demand she attest — meaning binding her identity permanently into the record. She realizes 'witness' means giving up her memories, her selfhood, to authenticate the truth. Emotional beat: the theme of belonging arriving at its cruelest price.

chapters.title: Forty Days, Spent
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, dissolving. She uploads herself alongside the message — childhood, her mother, the long years, Cassian — and speaks the attestation as her memories stream away. The broadcast fires across the whole system. Emotional beat: transcendence through surrender; love stated in the act of letting go.

chapters.title: Silence, Then Answer
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Across every screen in the system, the ceasefire key unlocks and the Vessic fleet stands down; Vane's forces fracture when soldiers hear the suppressed recordings. Cassian carries Elodie's empty body to the infirmary, refusing to call it death. Emotional beat: victory experienced as bereavement.

chapters.title: The Trial of Commander Vane
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV, months later. Vane stands trial; Cassian testifies using Elodie's archived testimony — her uploaded self, cross-examined as evidence. The war crimes surface fully. Emotional beat: justice achieved, but hollow without the witness in the room.

chapters.title: A Signal From the Deep
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. In the Archive's deep vaults, technicians find Elodie's pattern intact within the broadcast lattice — recoverable, if someone volunteers to host it. Cassian signs up without hesitation. Emotional beat: hope earned, not given.

chapters.title: Beacon Seven, Relit
chapters.summary: Shared POV, coda. Elodie wakes slowly, remembering everything and being slightly more than she was. They return to Beacon 7 together, relight the beacon as a monument to the peace, and stay — two keepers now, never relieved, no longer alone. Emotional beat: belonging chosen at last; the orbit closed.
